sections.section_title: Paul's Boasting and the Corinthians' Readiness
sections.summary: Paul notes that it is superfluous to write further about the collection since he already knows the Corinthians' readiness, and reveals he has been boasting about them to the Macedonians as a motivating example.

sections.section_title: The Practical Urgency of Sending Brothers Ahead
sections.summary: Paul sends delegates ahead to arrange the collection in advance so that it will be a willing gift (eulogia) rather than an exaction (pleonexia), protecting both his reputation and the quality of the giving.
Paul establishes the principle that bountiful sowing produces bountiful reaping, and that giving must be decided in the heart, not reluctantly or under compulsion, because God loves a cheerful giver.

sections.section_title: God's Ability to Supply and the Psalm of the Righteous Giver
sections.summary: Paul declares that God is able to make all grace abound so that the Corinthians may have sufficiency and abound in every good work, supported by the Psalm 112:9 citation identifying generous distribution to the poor as the righteousness that endures forever.

sections.section_title: God as the Supplier of Seed and the Multiplier of Righteousness
sections.summary: Drawing on Isaiah 55:10, Paul describes God as the one who supplies seed for sowing and bread for food, multiplying the harvest of the Corinthians' righteousness and enriching them for the purpose of generosity that produces thanksgiving.

sections.section_title: The Collection as Confession, Communion, and Glorification
sections.summary: Paul describes how the collection not only supplies the Jerusalem saints' material needs but also produces thanksgiving and glorification of God, demonstrates the Corinthians' obedience to their gospel confession, and creates a bond of longing and prayer between the communities.
Paul closes the collection argument with a doxological exclamation, declaring God's gift to be beyond the capacity of language to describe.
